To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of drugs which elevate cyclic AMP on contractility of cardiac muscle are due to the activation of protein kinase, and that the effects of these same drugs can be antagonized by muscarinic agonist by inhibiting the activation of protein phosphorylation.

the mechanism by which the positive inotropic drugs increase the force of contraction is to increase the amount of calcium available for contraction by increasing the calcium current and by inhibiting the calcium pump of the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which cyclic AMP-elevating drugs modify myocardial contractile state.
the cellular mechanisms of inotropic agents.
the cellular mechanism of action of inotropic agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we are still at an early stage of understanding how drugs which increase cyclic AMP level modify cardiac contractility.

the cellular mechanisms of positive and negative isotropic agents, which are based on the elevation of intracellular levels of cAMP, are still under investigation and that the results of the present study are preliminary and should be confirmed and extended.

the cyclic AMP-dependent protein kinase is a major, if not the major, mediator of the inotropic effects of the positive inotropic agents and that this kinase is also involved in the inotropic response of cardiac muscle to catecholamines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
drugs which elevate the intracellular levels of cAMP, such as the positive inotropic agents, act by phosphorylating a specific protein which in turn increases contractility.
cyclic AMP-dependent protein kinase is the final common pathway for drugs that elevate myocardial contractility by increasing cyclic AMP.
cyclic AMP-dependent phosphorylation of proteins in myocardial cells may represent a key step in the mechanism by which positive inotropic agents elevate contractile force.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cellular mechanisms of the inotropic agents are more complex than previously thought.
the cellular mechanism of action of positive inotropic agents is not as straightforward as it may appear.
cyclic AMP is a very potent positive inotrope and that it acts by a mechanism which involves the phosphorylation of a 22,000 dalton protein.
